pageCache.pageTitle: Breakfast Club Provisions - Bayards Hill Primary School
pageCache.text:
Breakfast Club Provisions
We offer two morning options to help families start the school day with a healthy meal and a safe, welcoming environment. Both clubs are fully staffed and supervised by our existing school team, ensuring your child is greeted by familiar, friendly faces every morning.
Both sessions must be booked in advance using the MyChildAtSchool (MCAS) app.
1. Our 'paid for' Breakfast Club from 8am
Start your day early with dedicated childcare and a full breakfast menu.
Time: 8:00am - 8:45am (Monday to Friday)
Cost: £1 per child, per session
2. Our Free Breakfast Club (DfE funded)
A free, nutritious breakfast session open to all eligible pupils.
Time: 8:15am - 8:45am (Monday to Friday)
Cost: Free (Funded by the Department for Education)
Both our Breakfast Clubs offer the following:
Breakfast: Choice of cereal, wholemeal toast with various spreads, fresh fruit, yoghurt, and fruit juice/water with a special menu on a Friday, which includes pastries, waffles, cooked breakfast.
Activities: Quiet games, craft stations, reading corners, and supervised outdoor play (weather permitting).
Drop-off and sign in: Please bring your child to the school office to be signed in.
Transition: At 8:40am, staff will escort children directly to their classrooms ready for registration.

pageCache.pageTitle: Headteacher's Welcome - Bayards Hill Primary School
pageCache.text:
Headteacher's Welcome
On behalf of all the pupils, parents/carers, staff and governors, it is my pleasure to welcome you to the website of Bayards Hill Primary School. As Headteacher, I am extremely proud and privileged to have worked in the school for over 12 years.
We are a one-form entry school providing academic and pastoral provision for over 240 pupils, from Nursery to Year 6. We promote the basic British values of: democracy, the rule of law, individual liberty, and mutual respect and tolerance for those of different faiths and beliefs. As part of our commitment to developing character, all staff, pupils and governors share and promote our three key values: Respectful, Responsible and Resilient.
We believe that a great education is built from positive relationships and strong partnerships between home and school. We recognise children as unique individuals with talents and needs that are nurtured through inclusive classrooms; where they can flourish and reach their full potential. We celebrate each other’s successes, and we support each other in overcoming obstacles and challenges.
Across our ambitious curriculum, we develop creativity, curiosity, initiative, independence and most importantly confidence and self-belief. This is enriched through the creative planning of unique experiences, educational trips and visits, and visitors to schools.
This website offers an insight into the amazing things that take place in our school. However, visits are highly encouraged and warmly welcomed: we would be delighted to show you around our wonderful school.

pageCache.pageTitle: Requesting Absence - Bayards Hill Primary School
pageCache.text:
Requesting Absence
Requesting absence due to exceptional circumstances
All schools can grant a leave of absence when a pupil needs to be absent from school with permission. All schools are expected to restrict leaves of absence to the specific circumstances set out in regulation 11 of the School Attendance (Pupil Registration) (England) Regulations 2024 and schools maintained by a local authority and special schools not maintained by a local authority must do so. These circumstances are:
• Taking part in a regulated performance or employment abroad: in line with a licence issued by a local authority or Justice of the Peace or a body of persons approval (BOPA). (For full details please see Code C1)
• Attending an interview: for entry into another educational institution or for future employment where requested in advance by a parent the pupil normally lives with.
• Study leave: for public examinations, as agreed in advance with a parent the pupil normally lives with. Please note this does not include any internal examinations such as mocks as study leave should not be granted in such cases.
• A temporary, time-limited part-time timetable: where the pupil is of compulsory school age, both the parent who the pupil normally lives with and school agree the pupil should temporarily be educated on a part-time basis for exceptional reasons and have agreed the times and dates when the pupil will be expected to attend school as part of that timetable. (For full details please see part-time timetable)
• Exceptional circumstances: All schools can grant a leave of absence for other exceptional circumstances at their discretion. In the case of schools maintained by local authorities and special schools not maintained by local authorities, it must be requested in advance by a parent who the pupil normally lives with. Schools are then expected to consider each application individually taking into account the specific facts and circumstances and relevant background context behind the request. If a leave of absence is granted, it is for the school to determine the length of the time the pupil can be away from school.
For more information please refer to the full statutory guidance below:
Working Together to Improve School Attendance
Please note - generally, the DfE does not consider a need or desire for a holiday or other absence for the purpose of leisure and recreation to be an exceptional circumstance. Leave of absence should not be granted for a pupil to take part in protest activity during school hours.
